body.p: Claims 1-10 are pending in the application. Reconsideration of the objection and rejections set forth in the aforementioned Final Office Action is respectfully requested in view of the above amended claims and following remarks. The basis for these amended claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed.

Applicant respectfully submits that the above amended claims overcome the current objection and rejections of record and, as such, all of the claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests completion of prosecution and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. However, should the Examiner elect to issue an Office Action in response to this Amendment After Final, Applicant hereby requests a telephonic interview with the Examiner prior to issuance of any Office Action in order to discuss any remaining issues.

Claims 1-3, 5-7 and 10 stand objected to because of various "informalities." Pursuant to the Examiner's suggestions and recommendations, amendments to Claims 1-3, 5-7 and 10 have been made in order to address the noted informalities.

Specifically, regarding the phrases "requiring care" and "having space necessary for care," Applicant respectfully submits that these phrases are clear and unambiguous from Applicant's specification. For example, page 8, lines 7-11 of Applicant's application provides "[t]hat is, the memory 62 or the like of the measure determination device 60 inputs information on the age of the passenger and whether or not the passenger is a person requiring care at the time of making a reservation for the unmanned autonomous

driving vehicle 10." That is, the individual making the reservation for the unmanned autonomous driving vehicle at the time of making the reservation knows whether or not the passenger is a person requiring care.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the objections to Claims 1-3, 5-7 and 10.

Claims 1-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as "being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention." Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection as it is Applicant's view that the claims as written fully comply with Section 112. However, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended Claims 1-10 pursuant to the Examiner's suggestions and recommendations. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 112(b) rejections to Claims 1-10.

Claims 1-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's characterization that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, renders Applicant's claimed disclosure obvious. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. It is respectfully submitted that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, teaches away from Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device. Applicant's claimed disclosure recites an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device having a unique and advantageous orientation and combination of components which are more efficient, advantageous, and eliminate various negative features associated with the devices/systems disclosed in the cited references.

Applicant's claimed disclosure is directed toward an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device which are capable of maintaining safety and appropriately providing relief to a failed autonomous driving vehicle. Applicant's improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device are able to accomplish these tasks as a result of their unique and advantageous arrangement and orientation of components and features which include, in part, the following:
a vehicle control device configured to

recognize a fault of an in-vehicle device used for autonomous driving in an autonomous driving vehicle or a temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device by monitoring an operation state of a signal transmitted from the in-vehicle device, and
receive information indicating the fault of the in-vehicle device or the temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device.

Specifically in this regard, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 set forth Applicant's unique and innovative arrangement and orientation of components, reciting a vehicle control system and a vehicle control device including, in part, a vehicle control device configured to "recognize a fault of an in-vehicle device used for autonomous driving in the autonomous driving vehicle or a temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device by monitoring an operation state of a signal transmitted from the in-vehicle device, receive information indicating the fault of the in-vehicle device or the temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device." Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest, at least, any structure similar to a vehicle control system and a vehicle control device including, in part, a vehicle control device configured to "recognize a fault of an in-vehicle device used for autonomous driving in the autonomous driving vehicle or a temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device by monitoring an operation state of a signal transmitted from the in- vehicle device, receive information indicating the fault of the in-vehicle device or the temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device" as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. There is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. In fact, the cited references teach away from and articulate various disadvantages associated with the arrangement, configuration and orientation of components taught in Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Poeppel et al. describes "[t]he remote computing system may determine that an autonomous vehicle is safe or suitable to continue with a vehicle service or is not safe or suitable to continue with a vehicle service", for example. Poeppel et al. broadly describes a determination that an autonomous vehicle is safe or suitable but does not describe any specific situation or detail.

Poeppel et al. does not disclose, teach or suggest, at least, a vehicle control device configured to "recognize a fault of an in-vehicle device used for autonomous driving in the autonomous driving vehicle or a temporarily unusable state of the in-vehicle device by monitoring an operation state of a signal transmitted from the in-vehicle device" as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure.
Wilson et al. describes a rendezvous coordination of an autonomous automotive vehicle with an ambulance.

As such, Applicant respectfully submits that Wilson et al. does not relate to the present application. Applicant's application relates to a technique for setting a safe stop position for an autonomous driving vehicle and causing the autonomous driving vehicle to stop at a position when a fault occurs in the autonomous driving vehicle. See Applicant's application at Background.
The term "relief method" does not relate to a medical emergency. This term has been removed from Applicant's claims to clarify/more clearly define the scope of Applicant's claims.
In a case where autonomous driving is impossible to continue, another vehicle (a second autonomous vehicle) goes to a position/location where the first autonomous
vehicle in which a person rides is present, or another position/location where the second autonomous vehicle and the first autonomous vehicle in which a person rides meet.

Thus, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. The deficiencies found in Poeppel et al. are not corrected by the combination of Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that amended independent Claims 1 and 6, and all claims depending directly or indirectly therefrom (Claims 2-5 and 7-10), are not obvious in light of and are patentable over Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's succinct arguments set forth above and previously, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, fails to disclose, teach or suggest several features that are recited in Applicant's claimed disclosure. As such, Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device are not disclosed, taught or suggested by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited.

Without conceding to the correctness of the Examiner's comments thereto, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2-5 and 7-10 are allowable, at least, for the same reasons given above for amended independent Claims 1 and 6, because Claims
2-5 and 7-10 are ultimately dependent on either independent Claim 1 or independent Claim 6.

It is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's arguments stated above and previously, Poeppel et al. is an improper primary reference, Wilson et al. is an improper secondary reference, and Applicant's claims are patentably distinct with respect thereto, as well as no teaching in existence to suggest the combination of any of the cited references. In the Final Office Action, the Examiner's conclusory statements are insufficient to establish a prima facie rejection because no articulated reasoning with rational underpinning was given, and no explanation as to exactly how the combination or modification could have been made was provided. As a result, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner has failed to identify any motivation by one of ordinary skill in the art to combine or modify the art to arrive at the claimed disclosure other than the impermissible use of hindsight.

While it is Applicant's view that the claims as written are not obvious in light of the cited art and fully comply with Section 103, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended independent Claims 1 and 6. Therefore, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 should be in condition for allowance. Further, because Claims 2-5 and 7-10 depend from either amended independent Claim 1 or amended independent Claim 6, directly or indirectly, they are at least as limited, are similarly not taught by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, and should also be in condition for allowance. In view of the above
amendments and these remarks, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 103 rejection to Claims 1-10.

All of the stated grounds of objection and rejection have been properly traversed, accommodated or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider all presently outstanding objections and rejections and that they be withdrawn. It is believed that a full and complete response has been made to the outstanding Final Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Thus, prompt and favorable consideration of this Amendment After Final is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes that personal communication will expedite prosecution of this application, they are invited to contact the undersigned at their earliest convenience.
